sections.title: 一、完形填空
sections.instruction: 阅读短文，从各题所给的四个选项中选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。
sections.passage:
Getting along with people around you is a key to happiness. In everyday life, whether with parents, teachers, or friends, how we get on with others really matters. A good [1] makes our days brighter and helps us grow. Here are some simple and [2] ideas.

First, try to [3] more often. A smile makes you look warm. When you see classmates in the playground, just smile and say hello. It makes them feel good, and they will enjoy being with you.

Second, learn to be a good [4]. When others talk, stop what you're doing, look at them, and listen carefully. This shows that you care about what they are saying.

Third, be [5] and ready to help. Small acts of kindness mean a lot. If someone can't find his/her eraser, lend him/her yours. You can also help a friend with a math problem. [6] help brings you closer to your friends.

Fourth, know how to say sorry when you are wrong. Everyone makes [7], but saying sorry can solve problems. Also, try to forgive (原谅) others when they say sorry.

Finally, don't [8] others when you disagree. Instead, talk in a friendly way, stay calm, and try to [9] how they feel.

If you follow these pieces of advice, you can build [10] and lasting friendships. Wish you a happy time with people around you!

questions.translation: 一段良好的人际关系会让我们的日子更美好，并帮助我们成长。
questions.explanation: 根据前文 'how we get on with others really matters'（我们如何与他人相处至关重要）可知，此处指良好的人际关系（relationship）。故选 relationship。

questions.translation: 这里有一些简单且有帮助的想法建议。
questions.explanation: 下文列举了有助于与他人更好相处的实用建议，所以这些想法是有帮助的（helpful）。故选 helpful。

questions.translation: 首先，尽量多微笑。
questions.explanation: 后句紧接着提到 'A smile makes you look warm.'（微笑让你看起来温暖），因此首个建议是多微笑（smile）。故选 smile。

questions.translation: 其次，学会做一个好的倾听者。
questions.explanation: 根据后句 'When others talk, stop what you're doing, look at them, and listen carefully.'（当他人说话时，停下手中的事并认真倾听）可知，是要做一个好的倾听者（listener）。故选 listener。

questions.translation: 第三，保持积极并乐于助人。
questions.explanation: 根据后文 'and ready to help. Small acts of kindness mean a lot.' 可知，是要保持积极友善（positive）的态度并乐于助人。故选 positive。

questions.translation: 提供帮助会拉近你和朋友之间的距离。
questions.explanation: offer help 意为“提供帮助”，动名词形式 Offering 作句子主语。故选 Offering。

questions.translation: 每个人都会犯错，但道歉能够解决问题。
questions.explanation: make mistakes 为固定搭配，意为“犯错误”。故选 mistakes。

questions.translation: 最后，当你不同意他人观点时，不要与他人争吵。
questions.explanation: argue with 意为“与……争论/争吵”，与后文 'talk in a friendly way, stay calm'（友好沟通、保持冷静）形成对比。故选 argue with。

questions.translation: 相反，以友好的方式交流，保持冷静，并尝试去理解他们的感受。
questions.explanation: understand how they feel 意为“理解他们的感受”。故选 understand。

questions.translation: 如果你遵循这些建议，你就能建立牢固而持久的友谊。
questions.explanation: strong and lasting friendships 意为“牢固且持久的友谊”，strong 与 lasting 并列修饰友谊。故选 strong。

sections.title: 二、阅读理解 A
sections.instruction: 阅读短文，从各题所给的四个选项中选出最佳选项。
sections.passage:
Last Friday, I took a crowded subway to work, feeling a little low. As the doors closed, a cheerful voice came from the train speaker (扬声器), "Good morning. Welcome to this train! Wish you a happy journey!" It was such a lovely voice that I looked up and caught the eye of another passenger.

I smiled, and the woman smiled back. Then we did something that people hardly do on a crowded subway—we started talking.

"Oh, I love this voice!" said my eye-contact (眼神交流) friend.

"Cheerful and warm!" I replied.

When I got off the train, I felt lighter. And the good feeling stayed with me all day.

What happened? Could the cheerful voice and the short talk with a stranger have changed my feelings? "Yes," said researchers. In their research, Gillian Sandstrom and Elizabeth Dunn suggested that talking to people you don't know well—people with "weak ties (联系)"—can make you happier.

To test this idea, they asked students to count how many times they talked with classmates in person. The students who had more face-to-face conversations—even small ones with people they never knew—said they felt happier.

Next, Sandstrom and Dunn asked students to write down all their social talks for three days. They used two notebooks: one for "strong-tie" talks and one for "weak-tie" talks. The results showed that people who had more "weak-tie" talks felt happier than others.

So, just say hello to the policeman on the corner, the kid with the cute dog, or the new neighbor. It might make you feel better than you expect.

questions.prompt: How does the writer lead in the topic in the first paragraph?
questions.translation: 作者在第一段是如何引入主题的？
questions.explanation: 第一段通过描述上周五乘地铁去上班并听到广播、与陌生人眼神交流并交谈的个人经历来引入话题。故选 By sharing an experience。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the researchers find about "weak-tie" talks?
options: "Weak-tie" talks had no effect on people's feelings.
People having more "weak-tie" talks became less friendly.
People having more "weak-tie" talks felt happier than others.
questions.translation: 根据文章，研究人员关于“弱联系”交流有什么发现？
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段 'The results showed that people who had more "weak-tie" talks felt happier than others.' 可知，有更多弱联系交谈的人感觉比其他人更快乐。故选 People having more "weak-tie" talks felt happier than others。

questions.prompt: What does the passage mainly talk about?
options: A day on the crowded subway.
Talking to a stranger makes one happy.
questions.translation: 这篇文章主要讲了什么？
questions.explanation: 全文通过地铁上的经历以及科学家的研究，阐述了与不太熟悉的人或陌生人进行简短交谈（弱联系）能让人感到更快乐。故选 Talking to a stranger makes one happy。

sections.title: 三、阅读理解 B
sections.instruction: 阅读短文，从各题所给的四个选项中选出最佳选项。
sections.passage:
A recent survey (调查) was carried out among young Chinese people. It shows that young Chinese are less good at expressing thoughts and ideas. Half of those young people said they had poor verbal skills (口头表达能力). And 40% of them said they had trouble expressing themselves well in writing.

Poor education could be a reason for poor communication skills, but that may not explain everything. Of the 1,333 young people, most were well-educated. The problem more likely came from the rise of digital (数字的) communication, with texting instead of talking, and short messages instead of long, complete sentences.

Today, having trouble expressing thoughts and ideas is a global problem. In America, some people try to work out the problem by returning to so-called "Classical Education". This kind of education took place about 500 years ago in Europe. They learn grammar, rhetoric, and logic. Grammar meant learning how to write a complete and correct sentence. Rhetoric was the use of grammatical devices (语法手段) to make one's writing better. And logic was the use of reason (理性) to identify what is true or not true.

If you want to improve your communication skills, [blank]. You can talk with others about books, the latest news, or even hobbies in this group. You can also get a beautiful diary and write down your thoughts in it every day. This will help you have a clearer mind so that you can express your ideas and feelings more clearly.

questions.prompt: If 100 young people are surveyed (被调查), how many more people have poor verbal skills than writing trouble?
questions.translation: 如果有100名年轻人接受调查，口头表达能力差的人比写作有困难的人多多少？
questions.explanation: 根据第一段 'Half of those young people said they had poor verbal skills (50%). And 40% of them said they had trouble expressing themselves well in writing.'，100人中口头表达差的有50人，写作有困难的有40人，相差 50 - 40 = 10 人。故选 10.。

questions.prompt: What does the underlined word "identify" in Paragraph 3 mean?
questions.translation: 第3段中画线单词“identify”是什么意思？
questions.explanation: 根据上下文 'logic was the use of reason to identify what is true or not true'，逻辑是运用理性来辨别/找出（identify/find）真伪。故选 Find。

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be put in "[blank]" in Paragraph 4?
options: you can join or start a discussion group
it's good to pick up new hobbies
keeping a handwritten diary may help
try to learn more about speaking
questions.translation: 以下哪一项可以填入第4段的空格处？
questions.explanation: 根据后句 'You can talk with others about books, the latest news, or even hobbies in this group.' 中出现 'in this group'（在这个小组中）可知，前一句应提到加入或建立一个讨论小组（join or start a discussion group）。故选 you can join or start a discussion group。

questions.prompt: What is the best title for the passage?
questions.translation: 这篇文章的最佳标题是什么？
questions.explanation: 文章分析了现代年轻人表达能力下降的现状、原因以及改进表达能力的建议，Express Yourself Better（更好地表达你自己）最契合全文主旨。故选 Express Yourself Better。

sections.title: 四、阅读还原
sections.instruction: 阅读下面短文，从短文后的选项中选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。
sections.passage:
You may disagree with your family members or friends sometimes, and disagreements can be uncomfortable. How can we make conversations more polite and meaningful? [1]

### Listen to their side
Even if you don't share others' opinions, you can still listen to what they say. [2] It means really listening to what the other people are saying and trying to understand what the other people are feeling. Nodding your head or saying "I see" shows you care. In this way, they know you respect their feelings and understand them.

### Try respectful language
Some people argue with others by attacking (攻击) or making fun of them. [3] Here are some ways for you to express opinions with respect. For example, don't use impolite words like "stupid", and you might say "I feel" or "I see this in another way". This way, the other person won't feel attacked, and you can talk about the real problem.

### [4]
If you have a strong opinion, you may get angry. It's not a good time to talk. Getting angry and shouting will only make things worse. Don't let your emotions control the talk. Taking a step back to breathe can help you both think more clearly.

[5] It's just like learning English and you can try one tip at a time. You will find that talking and listening in these ways can make life with family and friends much happier and easier.
wordbank: This is more than just being quiet.
There are some steps you can take.
Remember, becoming a good communicator takes practice.
But such disrespectful ways of arguing can only cause fights.

questions.translation: 空格[1]填空
questions.explanation: 前句提出问题“我们如何让对话更礼貌更有意义？”，此处承上启下引出下文介绍的三个具体步骤（Listen to their side, Try respectful language, Stay calm...）。故选 "There are some steps you can take."。

questions.translation: 空格[2]填空
questions.explanation: 后句解释 'It means really listening to what the other people are saying and trying to understand...'，说明倾听不仅仅是保持安静（more than just being quiet），而是要真正去理解对方。故选 "This is more than just being quiet."。

questions.translation: 空格[3]填空
questions.explanation: 前句提到有些人通过人身攻击或嘲讽来与人争论，本句指出这种不尊重的争论方式只会引起冲突打斗（cause fights），随后引出使用尊重语言的建议。故选 "But such disrespectful ways of arguing can only cause fights."。

questions.translation: 空格[4]填空
questions.explanation: 该处为小标题，后文围绕不要发脾气、大喊大叫，深呼吸保持头脑清醒展开，因此小标题是“在争论中保持冷静”。故选 "Stay calm during arguments"。

questions.translation: 空格[5]填空
questions.explanation: 后文提到 'It's just like learning English and you can try one tip at a time.'，说明成为优秀的沟通者就像学英语一样需要不断练习（takes practice）。故选 "Remember, becoming a good communicator takes practice."。

sections.title: 五、语法填空
sections.instruction: 阅读下面短文，在空白处填入1个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。
sections.passage:
Having a good talk with others is an art. Before starting a chat, you can prepare some simple topics to avoid awkward (令人尴尬的) silence. When talking to someone, speak [1] (clear) so they can understand you easily. It's also important to be polite—don't interrupt (打断) others while they [2] (speak).

A good conversation needs both speaking [3] listening. Try to be a kind listener and show you care [4] their ideas. If you feel nervous at first, take a deep breath and [5] (relax). You can share small stories about your life, but don't talk only about yourself—ask them questions too.

Avoid talking about [6] (person) things like family arguments unless they bring them up. If the topic becomes boring, you can change it to something more interesting, like a new book or a funny video. Remember [7] (keep) a smile and make eye contact—these small actions will make the chat enjoyable.

After the talk, you might feel happy because you've made a [8] (connect). With practice, you'll get better at [9] (communicate) and find that talking to others is not as hard as you think. So next time, don't be afraid [10] (start) a chat—it could lead to a new friendship.

questions.translation: 和别人说话时，说得清楚一些，以便他们能容易理解你。
questions.explanation: 修饰动词 speak 作状语，应用副词 clearly。故选 clearly。

questions.translation: 当别人正在说话时不要打断。
questions.explanation: while 引导时间状语从句，表示某动作正在进行，主句是一般现在时的祈使句，从句应用现在进行时 are speaking。故选 are speaking。

questions.translation: 一次好的对话既需要表达也需要倾听。
questions.explanation: both... and... 为固定搭配，意为“既……又……”。故选 and。

questions.translation: 尽量成为一个和善的倾听者，表明你在乎他们的想法。
questions.explanation: care about 为固定搭配，意为“在乎，关心”。故选 about。

questions.translation: 如果你一开始感到紧张，深吸一口气并放松下来。
questions.explanation: and 连接两个并列的祈使句动词原形（take... and relax...）。故选 relax。

questions.translation: 避免谈论私人的事情，比如家庭争吵……
questions.explanation: 修饰名词 things 作定语，应用形容词 personal（私人的，个人的）。故选 personal。

questions.translation: 记得保持微笑并进行眼神交流……
questions.explanation: remember to do sth. 意为“记得去做某事”（动作尚未发生），remember doing sth. 意为“记得做过某事”。此处提醒记得保持微笑，应用不定式 to keep。故选 to keep。

questions.translation: 交谈之后，你可能会感到开心，因为你建立了一种联系。
questions.explanation: 冠词 a 之后应用名词形式 connection（联系），make a connection 建立联系。故选 connection。

questions.translation: 通过练习，你会更擅长交流……
questions.explanation: be good/better at doing sth.，介词 at 后面接动词时应用动名词形式 communicating。故选 communicating。

questions.translation: 所以下一次，不要害怕开启一次闲聊——它可能会带来一段新的友谊。
questions.explanation: be afraid to do sth. 意为“害怕/不敢做某事”，后接动词不定式 to start。故选 to start。
